title: Probe ablation winsplit - model onboarding notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal memo capturing a focused ablation-style bakeoff we ran to decide which 13B-ish variant to onboard for the next hosted channel (low-latency interactive assistant). This is not the full onboarding PR; it's a compact decision note with the experimental design, aggregated win/losss, and pragmatic rollout recommendation.

Executive summary:
- Compared 3 candidate variants across edge-case-heavy prompt slices using a winsplit (pairwise win/loss) human evaluation and automated signal probes.
- N = 600 human pairwise comparisons (stratified across 6 prompt types), bootstrap CIs computed.
- Winner by human preference: rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K (win-rate vs runner-up = 58.7%, p < 0.01).
- Tradeoffs: rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K shows +8–12% reduced token-cost vs rw-13b-v1 (8-bit execution) and 40–60ms median latency improvement under our dedicated infra profile. However it has a slight uptick in factuality regression on long-context summaries (hallucination-rate +1.6pp absolute).
- Recommendation: onboard rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K as the default for low-latency interactive assistant with a staged canary (5% -> 25%) and tight regression monitors on hallucination and rerank rate.

Experiment setup (short):
- Candidates:
  * rw-13b-v1 (baseline, FP16 optimized kernels)
  * llm-lite-12b (sparse-attn variant) - used to stress long-context behavior
  * rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K (new quantized runtime + micro-kernel selection)
- Dataset: mixed 1800 prompts sampled from production anonymized traffic + synthetic edge cases (total 2400 prompts, split into 6 prompt groups). We then sampled 600 prompts for pairwise human evals ensuring equal representation across groups.
- Prompt groups (labels used in analysis):
  1) short-answer (FAQ style)
  2) multi-step reasoning (2–4 steps)
  3) code transformation (short snippets)
  4) long-summary (500–750 tokens context)
  5) conversational context (3+ turns)
  6) safety/abuse probes (adversarial)
- Evaluation modalities:
  1) Pairwise human preference (A/B) with 3 annotator majority; win/loss/tie recorded. Instructions emphasized helpfulness, factuality, and brevity where appropriate.
  2) Automated metrics: embedding-similarity to reference, BLEU/ROUGE for code and summaries, hallucination heuristic (entity hallucination detector), latency (p50/p95) under standard infra load.
  3) Cost model: tokens * infra unit price (our internal cost-per-token proxy).
- Statistical testing: bootstrap of pairwise win-rate, pairwise significance via two-sided bootstrap (10k resamples). We flag p < 0.05 as significant.

Aggregate results (human pairwise winsplit):
- Pairwise table (columns: A vs B => A win-rate)
  rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K vs rw-13b-v1 => 58.7% (CI 55.1–62.3), p < 0.01
  rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K vs llm-lite-12b => 62.2% (CI 58.6–65.8), p < 0.001
  rw-13b-v1 vs llm-lite-12b => 53.1% (CI 49.2–56.9), p = 0.08 (not significant)

Per-prompt-group win-rate (rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K vs best alternative):
  short-answer: 51.5% (close; parity on clarity)
  multi-step reasoning: 61.9% (clear win)
  code transformation: 63.8% (better formatting + fewer mis-synthesized tokens)
  long-summary: 48.3% (loses on hallucination-sensitive long contexts)
  conversational context: 59.4% (better context continuity)
  safety/abuse probes: 55.6% (slightly better refusal / safety behavior)

Automated metrics summary (relative to rw-13b-v1 baseline):
  - Embedding sim (mean): rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K +0.9 pp
  - Hallucination rate (entity-level detector): +1.6 pp on long-summary bucket (absolute)
  - Latency p50: -45 ms (measured on dedicated infra config: 2xA10s, batching=auto)
  - Token cost: -9% token * infra unit price (due mostly to quantized execution and shorter outputs on average)

Important qualitative notes from annotators (selected):
  - multi-step reasoning: rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K produced clearer intermediate steps and fewer “logic leaps”.
  - long-summary regressions are concentrated on hallucinated numeric facts and invented references (often minor but visible).
  - code transformation: rw-infer-13b-v2-q4_K produced more consistent formatting, but struggled with one-off obscure language constructs present in the synthetic set.
  - safety probes: both variants handled direct abuse well; llm-lite had more evasive wording in some prompts.

Ablation mini-experiments (fast probes we ran inside the bakeoff):
  - KV cache disabled vs enabled: enabling KV cache improves multi-step reasoning win-rate by ~7pp for all variants (we keep KV cache on by default).
  - Quantization knobs: q4_K with per-op kernel selection gives best perf/cost; q8 variants reduce hallucination slightly but double latency in our infra (not acceptable for low-latency target).
  - Temp/top_p sweep: reducing temp from 0.8 to 0.3 reduces hallucination on long-summary by ~0.8pp but increases terse/omission complaints in short-answer group. We recommend not changing sampling defaults globally; consider route-specific overrides.

Rollout recommendation and triggers:
  - Stage 0: internal shadow testing + internal dogfooding (2 weeks) + extended automated checks on our eval harness.
  - Stage 1 (Canary 5%): 48h initial pass (collect human-in-the-loop failures for examples flagged by hallucination detector).
  - Stage 2 (Ramp 25%): 7 days, monitor metrics continuously.
  - Full roll: if stable for 7 days at 25% with no alert triggers.

Alert / rollback triggers (immediate rollback if any met):
  * global drop in human preference vs baseline > 5pp over 24h window (sampled A/B checks)
  * hallucination detector firing rate +2pp absolute sustained for 24h vs baseline
  * p95 latency regression > 25% or p50 > 100ms absolute increase under live traffic profile
  * error rate (runtime errors / OOM) > 0.05% sustained

Open questions & follow-ups:
  1) Can we tune the long-summary behavior with a targeted prompt-template (few-shot system prompt that forces source-citation)? Quick test: we ran a micro-probe that reduced hallucination by ~0.9pp. We should run this template on Stage 0.
  2) Should we maintain two model families (long-context optimized vs low-latency optimized) and route by prompt metadata? Ops cost increases but might reduce risk. Ops: estimate incremental infra cost vs user quality gain.
  3) Annotator error analysis: disagreement concentrated in borderline helpfulness vs verbosity decisions. We should run a 200-item adjudication to refine the rubric.

Appendix: quick wins for onboarding checklist (pragmatic):
  - Add canary dashboards: per-prompt-group win-rate, hallucination detector rate, latency p50/p95, cost burn rate.
  - Add automated rerank fallback: if hallucination detector above threshold, route to fp16 rw-13b-v1 until resolved.
  - Add per-route sampling override to reduce sampling temp for long-summary route.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally focuses on the human winsplit and practical rollout guards. Full onboarding PR will include model card, intention taxonomy, privacy review, export controls, and full perf benchmarks under more infra configs (GPU types).
- If you want the raw pairwise labels and per-annotator notes, see linked Confluence file and the PR above (JIRA-ML-1217).

Signed-off-by: Maya Chen (eng-applied-ml)
